extracted.intended_audience: Heads of Executive Departments and Agencies (federal agency leadership)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for federal agency leaders on implementing OMB Circular A-76 policies and procedures for deciding whether commercial/industrial type activities should be performed in-house or contracted out. Focuses on cost comparisons, workforce effects, organizational efficiency, and procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Least cost determination (contract vs in-house)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining the least cost method of providing essential services (contract or in-house).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Circular's Cost Comparison Handbook to perform rigorous comparisons of contract costs versus in-house costs to decide whether work will continue to be performed by in-house personnel or converted to a contract operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on competitive private enterprise
rubrics_metrics.description: This Administration strongly supports the general policy of reliance on competitive private enterprise to supply the products and services needed by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When private performance of commercial or industrial activities is feasible and no overriding factors require in‑house performance, agencies should consider contracting subject to the cost-comparison process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamline organizations for efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Streamlining existing government organizations ensuring they are organized and staffed for the most efficient performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational and staffing changes should be made to achieve the most efficient performance of commercial/industrial type activities as part of implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce long-range fiscal obligations when cost-effective
rubrics_metrics.description: Reducing long-range fiscal obligations through reductions in the Federal workforce when cost comparisons show a contract operation is more cost effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workforce reductions are an allowable outcome only if the cost comparison demonstrates that contracting yields greater cost-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance productivity via measurable job standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhancing productivity through the development of measurable job standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop measurable job standards to improve productivity and to provide objective bases for comparisons and performance evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous cost comparison using the Cost Comparison Handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: A rigorous comparison of contract costs versus in-house costs will be made, using the Circular's Cost Comparison Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook is the prescribed tool; follow its procedures and assumptions when conducting the comparative analysis to determine conversion decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum 10% savings threshold for conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing in-house activities will not be converted to contract performance on the basis of economy unless it will result in a savings of at least 10 percent of the estimated Government personnel costs for the period of the comparative analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit numeric minimum savings requirement — conversions based on lesser savings are not authorized under the Circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of first refusal for displaced Federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal employees displaced as a result of the conversion to contract performance will be given the right of first refusal for employment openings in the contract operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circular contains provisions giving appropriate consideration to affected employees; contracting decisions must account for these employee protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use contracting to circumvent personnel ceilings
rubrics_metrics.description: The instructions preclude the use of contracting with firms and institutions outside the Government solely to circumvent personnel ceilings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB Circular A-76 and instructions limiting civilian employment are complementary; agencies must contract only because it is cost effective, not to evade personnel limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for senior leadership, support, and timely implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation has lacked requisite leadership and support from agency officials; agency heads must become vigorously involved and provide overall leadership to fully implement the Circular by the close of fiscal year 1982.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency leadership commitment is essential for effective implementation; OMB will issue a Bulletin to provide visibility and assistance. Effective implementation requires agency-level stewardship and timely action.
